name: io.github.2016judea/breach-to-claim
title: Breach to Claim: data breach settlements
description: Am I owed money from a data breach? Open settlements, deadlines, payouts and official claim sites

tools.name: find_breach_settlement
tools.description: For 'I got a data breach notice from X', 'am I owed money from the X data breach', 'is there a settlement for X', 'how do I claim the X settlement', 'is this settlement letter real'. Matches the company against open class-action data-breach and privacy settlements, each read off its official court-authorized website: the claim deadline and days left, what it pays (documented losses up to $X, cash payment, credit monitoring), the class definition verbatim so the person can see if they are in it, whether the code printed on the notice letter is needed, the case and court, the official claim site, and a link to a page with their claim checklist filled in. If no settlement is open it says so, and lists the breach notices on public record (California and Washington AG) so the person knows the breach is real and to keep the letter. It takes the company name only: no Social Security number, notice ID, claim ID or name is needed or taken. This tool never files a claim; the person files on the official site and signs it themselves.

company.description: The company or organization named on the breach letter or in the news, e.g. 'Columbia University', 'DaVita'. Nothing else about the person.

state.description: Optional: the person's US state as a 2-letter code, when they mention it. Some settlements pay a state subclass more.

got_notice_letter.description: Optional: true if they received a notice letter or email about the breach or the settlement, false if not.

had_out_of_pocket_losses.description: Optional: true if they paid money or lost time because of the breach (fraud, credit freeze fees, hours spent), false if not.

tools.name: list_open_breach_settlements
tools.description: Every open class-action data-breach (and privacy/tracking-pixel) settlement we have read off its official website, sorted by claim deadline: company, deadline and days left, the most cash it pays, whether receipts are needed, and the official site. Use for 'what data breach settlements can I claim right now', 'which settlements close this week', 'data breach settlements with no proof required'. Refreshed daily; each row says when its official site was last read.

closing_within_days.description: Only settlements whose claim deadline is within this many days

kind.description: data_breach (default all) = stolen or exposed data; privacy_tracking = a website shared data through tracking pixels

no_documents_option.description: true = only settlements with a cash option that needs no receipts

tools.name: breach_settlement_details
tools.description: Everything read off one settlement's official website: the class definition and any subclasses verbatim, each benefit with its cap and whether documents are needed, the claim, opt-out and objection deadlines, the final approval hearing, the fund and class size when stated, the case, court, administrator and its contact, and the source page for each. Pass the slug from find_breach_settlement or list_open_breach_settlements.

tools.name: settlements_closing_soon
tools.description:
Open class-action data-breach and privacy settlements whose claim deadline falls within the next N days (default 14), soonest first: company, deadline, days left, most cash, whether receipts are needed, official claim site and page link.

Example questions:
- "Which data breach settlements close this week?"
- "What settlements are about to expire?"
- "Last chance class action claims this month"

tools.name: breach_settlements_no_proof_needed
tools.description:
Open settlements with a cash option that needs no receipts or documents, soonest deadline first, with the most cash, the official claim site and the page link.

Example questions:
- "Data breach settlements with no proof required"
- "Settlements I can claim without receipts"
- "Easy class action money I can claim now"

closing_within_days.description: Optional: only deadlines within this many days

tools.name: tracking_pixel_privacy_settlements
tools.description:
Open class-action privacy settlements where a website or app shared visitors' data with advertisers through tracking pixels or similar code, soonest deadline first, with what each pays and the official claim site.

Example questions:
- "Meta Pixel settlements I can claim"
- "Privacy class actions for hospital website tracking"
- "Settlements for websites that shared my data with Facebook"

tools.name: biggest_breach_settlement_payouts
tools.description:
Open settlements ranked by the most cash one person can claim (the cap stated on the official site), with the total fund and class size where the site states them. A cap is a maximum per claimant, not what everyone receives.

Example questions:
- "Which data breach settlement pays the most?"
- "Biggest class action payouts open right now"
- "Highest paying settlements I can still claim"

tools.name: is_this_settlement_letter_real
tools.description:
Checks a company's name against court-authorized settlements read off their official websites and against breach notices filed with the California and Washington attorneys general. Returns whether a matching settlement is open, its official web address and administrator, the case and court, and the breach notices on record, so the person can compare the address on their letter or email with the official one.

Example questions:
- "I got an email about a Columbia University settlement, is it legit?"
- "Is this class action letter a scam?"
- "Is the DaVita settlement website real?"

company.description: The company or organization named on the letter or in the news. Nothing else about the person.

tools.name: settlement_claim_deadline
tools.description:
The claim deadline and days left for a company's data-breach or privacy settlement, plus the opt-out and objection deadlines and the final approval hearing date, each as read off the official site.

Example questions:
- "When is the deadline for the Columbia settlement?"
- "Is it too late to file the DaVita claim?"
- "How many days left to claim the La Jolla Group settlement?"

company.description: The company or organization named on the letter or in the news. Nothing else about the person.

tools.name: how_much_will_i_get_from_settlement
tools.description:
What a company's settlement pays one person: each benefit with its stated cap and whether documents are needed, in the official site's own words, plus the total fund and class size where stated. Caps are maximums; the official wording shows whether payments can be reduced.

Example questions:
- "How much will I get from the Columbia data breach settlement?"
- "What does the DaVita settlement pay?"
- "Is the settlement payout worth claiming?"

company.description: The company or organization named on the letter or in the news. Nothing else about the person.

had_out_of_pocket_losses.description: Optional: true if they paid money or lost time because of the breach

tools.name: how_to_file_breach_claim
tools.description:
The person's claim steps for a company's settlement: whether the code on the notice letter is needed, which benefit fits their answers, what to gather, the deadline, and the official claim form link. The person files and signs on the official site.

Example questions:
- "How do I file a claim for the Columbia University settlement?"
- "I lost my notice letter, can I still claim?"
- "What do I need to claim the DaVita settlement?"

company.description: The company or organization named on the letter or in the news. Nothing else about the person.

got_notice_letter.description: Optional: true if they got a notice letter or email

had_out_of_pocket_losses.description: Optional: true if they paid money or lost time because of the breach

tools.name: did_company_have_data_breach
tools.description:
Breach notices a company filed with the California and Washington attorneys general since 2024 (date reported, breach dates, residents affected where stated, data exposed, source link), plus any open or closed settlement over it.

Example questions:
- "Did Kaiser have a data breach?"
- "Was my bank hacked?"
- "Has DaVita reported a breach?"

company.description: The company or organization named on the letter or in the news. Nothing else about the person.
